decisionsTitle: The past events have their own «Filtre», independent of the cards ahead (amending §602)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01 on QA:** «Mi-ar trebui aceleași filtre și pentru evenimentele din trecut». **And the same day, after §602 shipped:** «Am zis că vreau un filtru și la evenimentele trecute, la fel ca la cele curente».

**What §602 did, and why it was not what he meant.** §602 sent the listing's one filter state through the past section too: the top panel's ticks narrowed the cards ahead and the past window alike, the top panel read its offer off the past window as well, and a filtered page opened the past fold. Three things followed. There was one state for two lists, so a reader could not look for last spring's races without also hiding the runs ahead. There was no control at the past section itself — the «Filtre» button sat at the top of the page, far from the list it now also narrowed. And «Înscrieri deschise» was offered whenever any past event existed, because ticking it hid the past, which no reader means by "where can I register". The owner asked for a filter at the past events, like the one at the current events: a control of its own, with its own choices.

**Decision.**
- **Two scopes, one address.** The top panel keeps §413's parameter names (`type`, `surface`, `difficulty`, `distance`, `cost`, `partner`, `night`, `registration`). The past section's panel uses the same groups and flags under a `past-` prefix (`past-type`, `past-surface`, …, `past-registration`), read in both of §413's shapes — the form's repeated parameters and comma-separated values, any case, `-` for `_` (criterion 77). `events/domain/listing-filter.ts` gains `FILTER_SCOPES`, a pure `scopedParams(params, scope)` (the `upcoming` scope is the unprefixed names and ignores every `past-` name; the `past` scope is the `past-` names with the prefix stripped), `parseListingFilter(params, scope = "upcoming")` and `listingFilterQuery(filter, scope = "upcoming")`. `activeFilterCount` is unchanged. `?type=FOO` and `?past-type=FOO` still mean no filter.
- **Independent lists.** The cards ahead (the lead's included) and the undated section follow the upcoming scope alone; `matchingPastEvents` takes the past scope alone. The past heading, its `open`/`data-filtered` and its count follow the past filter alone: «Din trecut, după filtre (N)», «Din trecut — Concurs (N)» when one kind is all that is ticked, «N evenimente trecute» otherwise. The row the lead shows between seasons (§167) is still left out by its id.
- **Each panel offers its own rows.** The top panel's offer is back to the dated and the undated cards; §602's side effect — «Înscrieri deschise» offered because a past event exists — is gone. The past panel's offer is `offeredFilters` over the past window alone (less the lead's row), under §413's rule (criterion 75): a box only where ticking it narrows the past, or where the address ticks it. No past event has an open door, so «Înscrieri deschise» is not offered there unless the address ticks it. The past section's control does not follow criterion 75's rendering rule, and this is deliberate: the owner asked for a control at the past events, and a control that is absent whenever last season was uniform — which is the case on production, where the past window is one weekly series — reads as missing, not as honest. So the past panel renders whenever the section has at least one row (the lead's row left out), and with nothing to narrow and nothing ticked its fold holds one sentence instead of a form: «Toate evenimentele trecute sunt la fel — {values} — așa că nu e nimic de filtrat aici.» / "Every past event is the same — {values} — so there is nothing to narrow here." (`Events.filter.pastNothingToNarrow`), the values being the kind, the surface, the difficulty band, the distance band and the cost where every past event shares exactly one, joined with the locale's list formatting (`singleValues`). The «Filtre» button keeps its words and opens the fold (a native `<details>`, no script). The boxes' own rule stands — no box that narrows nothing — and the top (upcoming) panel keeps it untouched: it renders only when it offers something or the address ticks something (§413 criterion 75, and criterion 180 of §602, which said the panel offers a value the past carries, are amended for the past scope only). The live QA and production windows were not readable from the build session; the e2e seed's one past group run is a uniform window, which now shows the button and the sentence.
- **Its place and plumbing.** The past panel renders inside the past `<details>`, right after its heading and before the cards, so it is reachable only when the fold is open — and with a past tick the fold is open. `ListingFilterPanel` gains `scope` and `carry`: `carry` is the other scope's ticks, kept as hidden inputs in the form and in every chip link, so a tick in one panel — submitted natively or by `FilterAutoApply`, which builds the address from the form's own fields — keeps the other's. Its boxes, its «Scoate filtrul: …» links and its «Șterge filtrele» use the scope's names; its form is named «Filtrele evenimentelor trecute» / "Filters for past events" and its row of active chips «Filtre active pentru evenimentele trecute» / "Active filters for past events"; its button still says «Filtre (N)», counting its own scope. `FilterAutoApply` remembers which scope was ticked, so only that panel reopens after a remount (§549), and it reopens every fold around the panel too — a reader who unticks the past section's last box is not left with the section shut over the panel they were using. When a past tick matches nothing, the section stays, open, with its panel and «Niciun eveniment nu se potrivește filtrelor alese.»
- **The live twin.** A `past-` tick changes what the listing shows, so the listing's twin rule (`i18n/live-twin.ts`, §549/§577) is now "either scope ticks something". `?past-foo=1` and `?past-type=FOO` stay on the CDN.
- **The calendar is left alone.** It draws no past section: it reads the upcoming scope only, a `past-` name on a calendar address is not a twin, and its links drop it.

**Why one address with two scopes, not two addresses or a client state.** A link still says everything the page shows: a reader can share "last year's trail races" or bookmark it, the GET form still works with no script (criterion 79), and the twin rule stays one parser over one query. A prefix is the smallest change that keeps every existing address meaning what it meant.

**Why the lists are independent.** A panel that shows unticked boxes while another panel narrows its list would lie about what is in force. Each list now answers to the panel next to it, and each button counts exactly the ticks that narrow its own list.

**What stays.** The window: one cached read of the latest 60 past events, 12 cards shown, the same data-cache entry whatever is ticked, narrowed in memory (§413, §602) — no new query, no new cache key. The calendar. §267's closed fold when nothing is ticked in the past scope. The undated section follows the upcoming scope, as before.

*Rejected:*
- **No past panel when nothing narrows (this entry's first version).** The owner's complaint was exactly the missing control; on a uniform window it read as absent. A button that opens onto an honest sentence replaced it.
- **Two panels sharing one state** — the owner's words, «la fel ca la cele curente», ask for a control of its own with its own choices; two buttons over one state would each claim the other's ticks.
- **A panel beside the past heading, outside the fold.** The fold is closed by default (§267), and a control for hidden content misleads: ticking a box would change a list nobody can see.
- **A wider window or a pager.** §602's reason stands: either costs a read, and the calendar is the archive.

**Tests.** Unit `events/listing-filter.test.ts`: both scopes of `scopedParams`/`parseListingFilter` (the upcoming scope ignores `past-*`; the past scope reads `past-type` repeated and comma-joined, any case, `-` for `_`, kilometre and legacy aliases), `listingFilterQuery(filter, "past")` round-trips and is nothing to the other scope, `withoutValue` on a past filter, and the top offer no longer holds a box only the past carries (§602's test reversed, its reason kept in the comment). Unit `events/past-events-filter.test.ts`: a past filter narrows the past and leaves the cards ahead alone, and the other way round; the past offer comes from the window and never offers «Înscrieri deschise»; with a past tick the section is open, draws only the matches and says «Din trecut, după filtre (N)», «Din trecut — Concurs (2)» for one kind; an upcoming tick leaves it folded and whole; a past tick that matches nothing keeps the section, its panel and the way back; the past panel sits between the heading and the cards, its boxes are named `past-…` and its hidden inputs carry the upcoming scope; the top panel's hidden inputs carry the past scope and its chip links keep it. Unit `i18n/live-twin.test.ts`: `?past-type=RACE` is the listing's twin, `?past-foo=1` and `?past-type=FOO` are not, `?type=RACE` still is, and the calendar ignores `past-`. `theme/density.test.ts` records the panel's gap. E2E `listing-filters.spec.ts`, both projects: the bare listing's past fold always has the «Filtre» button, with boxes or the sentence whichever the window is; and from an address ticking two past kinds, the past panel unticks «Concurs» — the address carries `past-type=GROUP_RUN` alone, the heading says «Din trecut — Alergare de grup (N)», the cards ahead are untouched — then «Concurs» in the top panel narrows the cards ahead and leaves the past heading as it was. Unit `events/past-events-filter.test.ts` also covers a uniform window (button and sentence with the right values in both languages, no checkbox), a mixed one (boxes, no sentence) and no rows (no section). `FilterAutoApply`'s memory of the ticked scope (`ui/filter-reopen.ts`, unit `events/filter-reopen.test.ts`) now carries the address the tick goes to, so a later mount on another address ignores it; it is also spent after the commit that answers the tick, whichever panel asked, and dropped after ten seconds: a past panel that stopped rendering (its last box unticked over a window with nothing else to narrow) can no longer leave a stale "past" that opens a later past panel, reached from a shared link or the back button, unasked.
changelogLine: - **«Din trecut» has its own «Filtre»** — the past events get the same filter button as the current ones, with their own choices in the same address; filtering one list no longer changes the other. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criteria 75 and 180 (§602's). Given the listing, then the past section carries its own «Filtre» panel inside its fold, reading and writing the same groups and flags under `past-` names in the same address; its offer comes from the past window alone and the top panel's from the cards ahead alone; a tick in one scope never narrows the other list; a `past-` tick opens the fold, heads it «Din trecut, după filtre (N)» and makes the address a live twin; the calendar ignores the past scope. The past panel is drawn whenever the section has a row, independent of the offer: where nothing narrows and nothing is ticked its fold holds the sentence «Toate evenimentele trecute sunt la fel — {values} — așa că nu e nimic de filtrat aici.» / "Every past event is the same — {values} — so there is nothing to narrow here." and no box, while the cards ahead's panel still renders only when it offers something or the address ticks something (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
